subtopics.title: Upper Bhadra Project and Bhadra River
subtopics.summary: A trial run of the Upper Bhadra Project carried water from the Bhadra Reservoir to Gonur Lake in Chitradurga district through the Chitradurga Branch Canal. The development marks the start of the project's operational phase and meets a long-standing demand for reliable water in parts of central Karnataka. The project has been given National Project Status by the Union Government. The Bhadra river rises in the Western Ghats and eventually becomes part of the Krishna river system.

subtopics.title: Ladakh Special Constitutional Framework
subtopics.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs has proposed a new chapter under Article 371 to create a Special Constitutional Framework for Ladakh. The framework envisages a directly elected legislative body at the Union Territory level. This body is expected to receive powers over matters particularly important to the region, such as land, culture, language, forests and environment. Other areas of legislative authority applicable to Union Territories under Article 240 may also form part of the proposal.

subtopics.title: India's National Accounts Revision
subtopics.summary: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released India's revised National Accounts Series in 2026, with 2022-23 as the new base year. The revised series adopts double deflation for manufacturing gross value added along with several other methodological changes. National accounts give a systematic framework for measuring an economy's production, income, expenditure, consumption, investment, saving and external trade. The revision aims to reflect structural changes, newer data sources and updated methods, so that constant-price estimates better reflect the contemporary economy.

subtopics.title: Blue Bond and the Navier-Stokes Claim
subtopics.summary: India is set to enter the blue finance market through its first blue bond, issued by Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited with SBI Capital Markets as arranger. Blue bonds finance projects that sustainably use and protect marine and freshwater ecosystems and are a sub-category of green bonds. Separately, OpenAI has claimed that an internal AI model generated a proposed proof for the Navier-Stokes Existence and Smoothness Problem, reportedly verified using Lean. The problem is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems designated by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000.

quizzes.title: Blue Bonds and the Navier-Stokes Claim
quizzes.passage:
Financial markets are looking beyond conventional projects towards the health of the seas and rivers. A new category of debt instrument is emerging to pay for work that keeps marine and freshwater ecosystems usable and protected over the long term. India plans to join this market through a bond issued by a company that focuses on the maritime sector. The bond will be arranged by a bank's capital markets arm, which has been appointed as arranger. Governments elsewhere have already experimented with similar tools, so the idea is not entirely new.

Science also produced a headline this month. A technology company said that an advanced artificial intelligence model had produced a proposed solution to a long-standing puzzle about how fluids move. Such claims are checked with formal tools that test every step of an argument. The puzzle concerns the equations that describe the motion of water, air and honey, and it belongs to a small group of famous challenges that a mathematics institute has highlighted.

Those equations are not merely theoretical. Engineers rely on them when they design aircraft and automobiles, and scientists use them to predict weather and model currents in the ocean. Progress on the puzzle would therefore matter far beyond mathematics, and that is why the claim has drawn wide attention.

questions.q: India's proposed blue bond is best described as a sub-category of which broader instrument?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the blue bond as a thematic sub-category of green bonds.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Seychelles issued the world's first sovereign blue bond in 2018.
Reason (R): The issuance was associated with the World Bank's SWIOFish3 Project.
In the context of the above statements, which one of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the SWIOFish3 link is only an association and is not stated to explain the 2018 bond.

questions.explanation: Seychelles matches its 2018 sovereign blue bond, Belize its 2021 debt-for-ocean swap, SMFCL is the maritime NBFC and SBI Capital Markets is the arranger.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Navier-Stokes problem:
I. The fluid equations are based on conservation of mass and Newton's second law of motion.
II. The Clay Mathematics Institute designated this problem in 2000 as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems.
III. The fluid equations describe the motion of water and honey, but not air.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is false because the booklet says the fluid equations describe air as well as water and honey.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
A. Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited is India's first maritime sector-specific NBFC.
B. Ocean-current modelling is one of the applications of the fluid equations.
C. The Navier-Stokes problem was designated a Millennium Prize Problem in 2010.
D. Seychelles issued the world's first sovereign blue bond in 2019.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements A and B are in the booklet, while C (2010) and D (2019) contradict the booklet's dates.

questions.explanation: The booklet describes Lean as a computer-based proof assistant designed to check mathematical arguments step by step.

quizzes.title: Schemes, Events and Honours
quizzes.passage:
September brought a mix of schemes, events and honours. The country marked International Literacy Day with a national festival that focused on adults who never learned to read. The programme is meant to build basic reading, writing and calculating skills among learners who have passed the age of school, so that they can take part fully in public life.

Water also featured in the news. A major conference on water management brought together experts, officials and delegates to discuss solutions that can withstand a changing climate. The event is a flagship initiative of a central government ministry, and it has been rebranded for the current year.

In cinema, the nation's highest honour is named after a pioneer of Indian films. The award recognises an individual's outstanding contribution to the growth and development of Indian cinema. This year's recipient is a veteran actor from Karnataka, and he follows an earlier recipient from the same regional film industry.

Beauty pageants made headlines too. The Miss World contest crowned a new titleholder from the Dominican Republic at its latest edition, and the next edition has already been planned for a future year in another country. An Indian contestant secured a place among the top forty.
